messages:
oliver: hey folks 👋 first-week question: where do I grab a sandbox key vs a hosted/prod key? Also curious if sandbox keys have per-key concurrent connection limits or per-route quotas — i.e., will streaming many small responses hit a different limit than bulk generate calls?

rachel: welcome! sandbox keys are auto-provisioned and visible under Console -> Sandbox Keys. Hosted/prod keys are created by org admins in Console -> API Keys and are billing-enabled. Prod keys usually require an owner and sometimes a short security review for sensitive scopes.

oliver: got it. any details on concurrency/streaming limits specifically? my demo uses server-sent events and a lot of concurrent short streams.

devex-bot: short answer: sandbox enforces both per-key RPS and concurrent-stream limits. Typical new-hire sandbox defaults: 12 reqs/sec per key, burst window up to ~48 reqs/sec for a few seconds, and ~50 concurrent streaming connections per key. These are soft limits and vary by cohort. Streaming sessions consume a concurrent-connection slot until the stream closes.

eng-sre: to add: there are also per-route soft quotas (e.g., embeddings vs chat vs generate) and a per-org aggregated token cap. For demos with many small streams, the concurrent-stream cap is usually the first bottleneck.

oliver: thanks. how do I monitor this in real time so I don't get 429s mid-demo?

rachel: Console shows live request charts and a connection gauge for org admins. For quick checks, look at response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Stream-Connections, Retry-After. If your client sees a 429 with X-Stream-Connections at max, close idle streams and backoff.

eng-sre: pro tip: implement a simple client-side semaphore to cap concurrent streams (e.g., max 30) and queue the rest. Also exponential backoff for 429s (retry-after header). For demos we often request a temporary elevated demo key to avoid surprises.

oliver: how do I request that elevated demo key? and who approves hosted keys for CI use?

devex-bot: File a request at https://go/redwood-help -> choose "Sandbox/demo quota". For a time-limited demo we need start/end time, expected concurrent streams, and expected token volume. Ops/eng-sre usually issues short demo keys (10-60min). For hosted keys used in CI/pipelines, org admin creates the key and security reviews keys that touch customer data. Email security@redwood.com for that flow.

oliver: any examples for the client-side semaphore and curl quickcheck?

rachel: simple curl (non-streaming quick check):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"hello"}'
```
Client semaphore pseudo:
```
const MAX_STREAMS = 30
async function startStream(req) {
  await acquireSemaphore() // block if >= MAX_STREAMS
  const stream = openStream(req)
  stream.finally(() => releaseSemaphore())
}
```

eng-sre: also note sandbox keys auto-expire after 90 days of inactivity in some cohorts; check Console for expiry and claim promo credits if prompted. If a key expires, request a new sandbox key or ask an admin to reissue.

oliver: awesome, super helpful. last Q: can I see my remaining sandbox credits programmatically?

devex-bot: yes — org admins can call GET /v1/org/usage (admin token required) to see token/credit usage. For individual keys you can view usage in Console -> Sandbox -> Key details. If you need read access, ask an org admin to grant it.

oliver: perfect — I'll open a demo quota request with expected concurrent streams. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
